title: Differential geometry of curves and surfaces
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the geometry of curves and surfaces in space: parametrized curves, arc length, curvature and torsion, the Frenet frame, regular surfaces and tangent planes, the first fundamental form, the Gauss map and the second fundamental form, principal, Gaussian and mean curvature, Gauss's Theorema Egregium, geodesics, and the Gauss–Bonnet theorem.
primary_reading: Lecture Notes on Differential Geometry, volume I: Curves and Surfaces, by Mohammad Ghomi (free PDF)

weeks.2: Curvature, torsion and the Frenet frame
weeks.4: Plane curves, the rotation index and the four-vertex theorem
weeks.6: The first fundamental form: lengths, angles and areas
weeks.7: The Gauss map and the second fundamental form

blocks.deliverable: Compute the curvature and torsion of supplied curves.
Reconstruct a curve from its curvature and torsion.
Compute lengths and areas on a supplied surface.
Week 7 midterm; compute the curvatures of a surface of revolution.
Prove that no region of a sphere is isometric to a region of the plane.
Verify the Gauss–Bonnet theorem for a supplied surface.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Curvature atlas: compute the first and second fundamental forms, principal curvatures and Gaussian curvature of six surfaces (including a torus, a catenoid and a saddle), check each by numerical differentiation in plain Python, integrate the geodesic equations numerically on two of them, and verify the Gauss–Bonnet theorem for the torus with a written proof.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
